A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MATRIX work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, video-generation comparisons, ablations and a 31-participant human evaluation, including Tables 1–2 and Appendix F.4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds backbone analyses, an attention-direction ablation, qualitative generalization tests and training-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The CogVideoX mask conditioning, causal decoders and SGA/SPA objectives remain unchanged. Appendix C adapts layer selection to Wan's separate self-attention and cross-attention modules, excluding prompt-insensitive, near-zero-variance layers before selecting influential layers.

E1.justification: MATRIX-11K and the main 60-synthetic/58-real evaluation pairs are retained. v2 adds a dedicated qualitative subset in Figure 24, including robot-object, object-object and animal-animal scenarios. Non-contact and animal content already appeared to some extent in v1, so the entire category is not new.

E2.justification: The four main quantitative baselines remain unchanged. v2 adds direct Wan2.1-14B-I2V versus MATRIX comparisons in Figures 10 and 42–43; Wan's earlier appearance concerned metric diagnostics. Table 2 also replaces the layer-selection-only comparator with a text-to-video SGA variant.

E3.justification: The main evaluation sets, metrics and human-study design are retained. Added experiments use 60-layer HunyuanVideo and 40-layer Wan with 50 sampling steps, introduce an attention-direction control, and compare training costs with matched hardware, resolution and batch size. These extend the experimental settings without establishing that the original benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis through cross-backbone layer studies, Wan dummy-layer diagnostics, per-clip score distributions, non-human/non-contact case studies and a training-efficiency comparison. Table 2 adds text-to-video versus video-to-text supervision analysis but removes v1's isolated layer-selection-only ablation.

E5.justification: Appendix G.4 and Figure 22 newly report empirical per-clip score distributions and observed ranges through violin plots. This adds descriptive variability reporting, but does not establish additional repeated runs or introduce confidence intervals, significance tests or new seed information.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain their scores. Table 2 removes the layer-selection-only result with KISA/SGI/IF of 0.490/0.594/0.542 and adds text-to-video SGA results of 0.486/0.578/0.531. New backbone and scenario figures add substantial empirical findings, while Table 5 newly reports 24.43 versus 31.09 hours per epoch for LoRA-only and MATRIX.

T1.justification: The attention-map definitions, AAS, mask unions, alignment losses, guidance equation and InterGenEval formulas are retained. The new backbone analyses and filtering procedure do not introduce a new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and four headline contributions are retained. However, Section 6.4 and Appendix C broaden the applicability claim to model-agnostic, plug-and-play use, including Wan's separate attention modules, beyond v1's explicit applicability statement for DiTs employing joint 3D full attention.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking backbone architecture to dominant-layer locations, contrasting attention-direction supervision, and interpreting reliability and computational tradeoffs. Appendices A.2 and J substantially expand discussion of mask tracks versus flow, depth and point tracking, including coarse local-motion supervision. The original instance-count and small-mask limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses second-annotator spot checks on approximately 5% of accepted clips, settings for the additional backbones, and comparative per-epoch training costs. Core CogVideoX implementation details remain unchanged. The promised release expands to include the curation pipeline, but neither PDF establishes that the promised resources are available.

R1.justification: v2 prunes citations including Track4Gen, DiTCtrl and MotionDirector, and adds Unified Dense Prediction of Video Diffusion alongside discussion of alternative supervision modalities. The main positioning around interaction-aware attention analysis and mask-track alignment remains intact.

P1.justification: Existing prose is condensed and rephrased, particularly in the introduction, related work and method exposition, while the ablation narrative is revised. The main narrative order is retained; new appendix sections are inserted, limitations and future work are separated, and acknowledgments and an ICLR publication header are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds multiple backbone-analysis plots, a violin plot, generalization and Wan comparison panels, dataset illustrations and a training-cost table. The influential-layer plots are redrawn as line plots, Table 2 is restructured, and several displays move substantially, including v1 Figure 13 becoming main-text Figure 4.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a limited net gain in validation and transparency through cross-backbone analyses, the attention-direction ablation, broader qualitative scenarios, and cost/distribution reporting. The gain is constrained by qualitative-only Wan comparisons, removal of the isolated layer-selection ablation despite retaining its conclusion, and incorrect IQ percentage gains in Table 5.
